instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.

Peel the ginger and slice it. Halve the onion. Peel 10 of the garlic cloves and leave them whole. Cut the white parts off 3 of the scallions. Slice the rest of the scallions, greens and all, and set them aside for serving.
Put the chicken, the 10 whole garlic cloves, the ginger, onion, scallion whites and peppercorns in a large pot. Add 8 cups of cold water.
Bring it to a boil over high heat. Skim off the foam with a spoon.

Turn the heat to medium low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest part of a thigh, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear and the meat pulls from the bone.
Meanwhile, make the spicy sauce. Mince the last 2 garlic cloves. Stir them in a small bowl with the 3 tbsp gochugaru and the 1 tbsp tamari.

Transfer the chicken to a plate and let it cool for 5 minutes. Pull the meat off the bones and shred it into bite sized pieces. Throw the skin and bones away, or return the bones to the pot for the last 5 minutes if you like a richer broth.

Take 3 tbsp of the hot broth and stir it into the spicy sauce. Strain the rest of the broth into a bowl, then spoon off the fat from the top. Return the broth to the pot and bring it back to a simmer. Season with the 1 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Put rice in each bowl. Top with the shredded chicken and ladle the hot broth over. Serve with the sliced scallions and the spicy sauce on the side.
method_notes: Korean Bapsang is the lead (4.82 from 97 ratings): chicken simmered with a lot of garlic, ginger, onion, scallion whites and peppercorns, shredded, and served over rice with the broth and a gochugaru sauce on the side. It uses a whole chicken for 40 to 50 minutes; The Subversive Table allows bone-in thighs and drumsticks, which cook in about 30, so this version uses those to stay under 50 minutes. The Subversive Table also adds carrot and noodles, which are left out here. Tamari replaces the soup soy sauce to keep it gluten free, and the spicy sauce is kept at the table so the soup stays mild.
